reasons.realCost: Mailchimp's price is fixed to the contact-count band a business falls into, so the sticker price is the real bill for that band, but the SMS/MMS add-on and any overage-limit charge have no published rate to predict in advance.
reasons.pricingHonesty: Mailchimp publishes contact-band pricing and plan comparisons for Free, Essentials, Standard and Premium, but does not state a per-contact overage rate, an SMS/MMS credit price, or Pay As You Go pricing anywhere on its public site.
reasons.smallTeamFit: Mailchimp is built for self-serve setup with purchase-behavior segmentation and templates included even on its Free plan, and offers a 14-day self-serve trial on Essentials and Standard with no sales call.
reasons.doesTheJob: Mailchimp combines email marketing, automation flows and ecommerce personalization with 300+ integrations on every plan including Free, covering most of a small merchant's marketing-layer needs in one subscription.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Essentials and Standard bill month to month below 10,000 contacts with contact-export tools built in, though Mailchimp's comparison page flags overage charges without stating their size.
reasons.trackRecord: Mailchimp has operated continuously since 2001 and has been owned by Intuit since 2021, giving it one of the longest operating histories among small-business email tools.

basis: Mailchimp remains one of the easiest and most established email tools for a non-technical small-business owner, with a generous feature set even on its Free plan, but unpublished overage and SMS pricing cost it points on cost predictability and honesty.
method: Two separate AI passes (two runs of Anthropic's Claude over the same evidence, neither seeing the other's score) scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the mean of the two overall scores, rounded down. Pass scores: 3.8 and 3.7.
